Riley Park: hey team, jumping into my first night shift and hitting a couple onboarding snags — can't access the private runbooks (403) and my PagerDuty test went to email but no mobile push. who's best to ping for quick access? :wave:
Jordan Lee: welcome Riley! For runbooks, you need the git-runbooks team + Okta group sync. DM me your Okta username and I'll check. For PD, did you accept the invite and set mobile push in profile?
Riley Park: accepted PD invite, profile shows mobile push enabled. invite email is riley.park@redwood.com. Okta username is riley.park.
Marta Silva: resending PD invite and kicking an Okta sync for you now. :mailbox_with_mail:
OpsBot: PagerDuty invite resent to riley.park@redwood.com — click the link to join rotation.
Riley Park: clone error still: "fatal: unable to access 'https://git.redwood.com/runbooks/': 403"
Jordan Lee: run `curl -I https://git.redwood.com/runbooks` and paste headers. Also run `okta sessions get` to ensure active session.
Riley Park: headers show WWW-Authenticate: Okta; okta sessions get returns "no active session"
Marta Silva: added you to git-runbooks and forced an Okta group sync. try cloning again.
Riley Park: clone succeeded, thanks! PD mobile test still silent though — delivery log says delivered but mobile status is "silent"
Tom Benson: check mobile OS settings. On iOS go Settings -> Notifications -> PagerDuty -> Allow Critical Alerts. If company MDM blocks critical alerts, add a backup contact method (work phone) and enable email->sms fallback in PD.
Riley Park: company MDM shows "critical alerts disabled by policy". I added a work phone and enabled email->sms fallback. will that be reliable during night shift?
Tom Benson: email->sms is slower but ok as backup. Also enable PD audible fallback in Settings -> Notification Rules so critical alerts call your number if push doesn't sound.
Jordan Lee: quick triage checklist for your first response: 1) Acknowledge in PagerDuty, 2) run `runbook lookup <service>` to pull canonical steps, 3) post a one-line status to #incidents (sev|symptom|impact|action), 4) if no mitigation in 15 minutes escalate to L2 via `esc escalate --svc <svc>` or ping @sre-rotation. Keep messages terse.
Riley Park: noted. who merges runbook fixes? I found a small typo in the redis restart command while going through the playbook.
Marta Silva: open a docs PR on the runbooks repo labeled `docs: runbook fix`. Authors can open PRs; merging requires an L2 signer. If it's blocking recovery during an incident, paste the fix in the incident thread and ask an L2 for a quick merge with the `hotfix` label.
Riley Park: ok will do. also saw a calendar event "oncall shadow shift" — do I need to attend before I take pages?
Tom Benson: yes, new oncalls must complete the shadow session and the "Oncall Basics" lab. Shadow session pairs you with a senior responder for two shifts. After you finish the lab and two shadow shifts you'll get full escalation privileges. OpsBot will upgrade your PD role once requirements met.
OpsBot: Reminder: Complete "Oncall Basics" lab and attend two shadow shifts to unlock escalation privileges.
Jordan Lee: one more pro tip: run `runbook preview <svc>` before acknowledging if you need exact commands. And add the incident template to your clipboard: `sev | symptom | impact | mitigation | next steps` — paste that as your first message to #incidents.
Riley Park: last question — during a simulated outage lab, do we still file a postmortem?
Marta Silva: for sims, we do a short retro in the lab doc. Real SEV1/SEV2 incidents require a full blameless postmortem using the postmortem template in Confluence. Sims help practice comms and tooling, not formal postmortems.
Riley Park: perfect. thanks for the rapid help everyone, feeling much better about the night shift. :pray:
OpsBot: Scheduled: Oncall Shadow Session tonight 23:00 PT. Attendance recommended for new responders.
